title: Demonstrate Leadership Behaviors
coreMove: A team demonstrates leadership when pressure changes a real behavior: who is heard, what is escalated, which tradeoff is named, and how value stays protected.

exampleSpecs.domain: steering update preparation before any meeting action begins
exampleSpecs.audience: a project lead allocating scarce attention under professional standards
exampleSpecs.stakes: a leadership principle becomes a line on a slide or a live agenda choice
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: before execution starts, he allocates the final prep minutes to the decision evidence the principle requires

exampleSpecs.audience: a delivery lead facing two costly choices
exampleSpecs.stakes: the baseline can be protected only by hiding a risk, while escalation may damage trust in the date
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist faces the chapter's only explicit two-bad-options decision

exampleSpecs.domain: a project room discussing the PMBOK principle set
exampleSpecs.audience: a facilitator learning that authority is not the only source of leadership
exampleSpecs.stakes: expertise may stay unused if the room treats leadership as title-only
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: two named people let the lesson emerge through the exchange itself

exampleSpecs.audience: a project manager tempted to let the baseline color carry the meeting
exampleSpecs.stakes: a green report can hide the adoption work that makes the outcome valuable
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the reader expects baseline defense, then the outcome reveals the leadership behavior

exampleSpecs.domain: informal team message exchange before a project decision
exampleSpecs.audience: team members deciding how to use principle language without becoming stiff
exampleSpecs.stakes: a principle can stay ceremonial unless the next message changes a behavior
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: a compressed chat shows the lesson between the lines

exampleSpecs.domain: weekly variance review interrupted by a warning signal
exampleSpecs.audience: a PMO lead using a pause as the leadership technique
exampleSpecs.stakes: routine baseline defense can erase the tradeoff the project needs to confront
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: a routine gets interrupted, then the protagonist pauses and restarts differently
